name: firefly-swarm
summary: 225 additive DOM dots orbiting the pointer on a circle, each re-targeted four times a second with a 1-2s tween so the swarm never settles; press and hold and the whole thing blooms to a wider radius.

rows.description: Square root of the swarm size; the field holds rows squared particles. Upstream's rows.

frameRate.description: How many times a second each particle picks a new target. Upstream's createTimer frameRate. Lower it to thin the work on a busy page.

deviations.what: The wrapper's font-size: .2vh becomes 0.2cqh on the field's children, with container-type: size on the field itself.
deviations.why: Every length in the design is an em against that font-size -- the glow is 100em, each particle 5em -- so upstream is really sizing them as 20% and 1% of the WINDOW height. A section is not the window and can be any height, so the same two numbers are resolved against the section's own box instead. The proportions and the numbers are unchanged.

deviations.what: mousemove and mousedown listen on the section rather than the document, mouseup listens on window, and the pointer is measured from the field's centre instead of window.innerWidth / 2.
deviations.why: Upstream is a full-window demo where the document and the field are the same box, and it never unmounts. A section is one band of a page: a document listener would make a swarm two sections down chase a pointer that is nowhere near it. mouseup stays on window because a press released outside the section is still a release, and leaving it on the section would strand the swarm in its bloomed state.

deviations.what: Every createTimer is kept in a list, and destroy() cancels all of them, calls utils.remove() on the particles and the glow, and removes the particle elements.
deviations.why: Upstream creates 226 timers and never stops any, which is correct for a page that only unloads. Here a section can be torn down on a page transition, and a timer that keeps firing animate() on detached nodes is a leak that outlives the section. utils.remove() is needed specifically because composition: 'blend' means a new tween does not cancel the one still running, so several can be live per particle at teardown.

deviations.what: The three particle colours come from --fx-fly-1/2/3 rather than upstream's --red-1, --corail-1 and --orange-1, and utils.set() writes the colour AFTER the particle is appended rather than before.
deviations.why: Those variables are defined in the examples' shared assets/css/styles.css, which is not part of this port, so the values had to be chosen here. The picks keep the warm red-to-amber run the example reads as, and they are custom properties so a section can retune them. The reorder is a fix, not a preference: a var() reference resolves against the computed style and a detached element has none, so upstream's ordering writes an empty value and every particle falls back to the wrapper's inherited colour.

deviations.what: The grab / grabbing cursor from upstream's body rule only applies under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.
deviations.why: A grab cursor tells a reader that pressing does something. Under the preference mount() builds no swarm, so there is nothing to open and the cursor would be promising a behaviour that has been switched off.

deviations.what: A static resting cluster (.fx-fly__rest) is added under the same glow, and the copy sits on a --fx-scrim panel.
deviations.why: Effect contract: the section has to look finished with no script, and an empty dark field is not a section. The scrim is the contrast floor -- the live swarm is additive and crosses the copy, so text measured against the busiest frame needs a plate under it.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion no particles are built.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. The resting cluster is the finished section, so not building is the resting state rather than a downgrade.
